message.content:
**How to Boil an Egg (Perfectly Every Time)** | Step | What to Do | Why It Works | |------|------------|--------------| | 1. **Choose the Right Eggs** | Use eggs that are at least 2–3 days old (fresh eggs are harder to peel). | Older eggs separate more easily from the shell. | | 2. **Bring to Room Temperature** | Let the eggs sit out for ~10 min before cooking. | Reduces cracking and gives a smoother texture. | | 3. **Use a Large Pot & Water** | Fill a pot with enough water to cover the eggs by about 1 inch. | Even heat distribution prevents hot spots. | | 4. **Add Salt or Vinegar (Optional)** | Add ½ tsp salt or 1 tbsp vinegar to the water. | Helps prevent cracks and makes peeling easier. | | 5. **Heat to Boiling** | Bring water to a rolling boil over medium‑high heat. | Rapid heat transfer cooks the egg quickly. | | 6. **Lower the Eggs Gently** | Use a slotted spoon to drop eggs into the water. | Prevents cracking from impact. | | 7. **Set the Timer** | Cook for 9–12 minutes depending on desired doneness:
• 9 min → soft‑set yolk (runny)
• 10 min → slightly firmer yolk
• 11 min → medium yolk
• 12 min → hard yolk | Precise timing yields consistent results. | | 8. **Ice Bath** | Immediately transfer eggs to a bowl of ice water for 5–10 min. | Stops the cooking process and makes peeling easier. | | 9. **Peel** | Tap gently on a counter, roll lightly, then peel under running water. | Water helps separate the membrane from the shell. | ### Quick Reference Table | Desired Doneness | Cooking Time (after water boils) | Result | |------------------|-----------------------------------|--------| | Soft‑set (runny yolk) | 9 min | Creamy, runny yolk | | Medium (slightly firm yolk) | 10–11 min | Slightly thickened yolk | | Hard (fully set yolk) | 12 min | Firm yolk, fully cooked whites | **Pro Tips** - **Use a timer**: Even a phone alarm ensures you don’t over‑cook or under‑cook. - **Avoid overcrowding**: Too many eggs can lower the water temperature and cause uneven cooking. - **Peel under water**: Running water helps lift the shell away from the egg. Follow these steps and you’ll consistently get the perfect boiled egg—whether you like it soft, medium, or hard!
